messages:
mike: Heads-up: ran into a weird auth/race on WSL2 where redwoodctl login sometimes writes creds to both the Windows credential helper and the WSL file cache, and localserve then oscillates between profiles. Repro steps at bottom. Anyone seen double-write races like this?

anya: ugh. Which redwoodctl version and how is the credential helper configured?

mike: redwoodctl v1.1.4, using the new creds helper that detects 'wincred' on PATH. I was trying to share a single profile between Windows and WSL so I pointed XDG_CONFIG_HOME -> /mnt/c/Users/mike/AppData/Local/redwood.

sam: mixing NTFS mounts + credential helpers is asking for trouble. What exactly happens when you login?

mike: flow:
1) `redwoodctl login --device-code --profile dev-wsl` from WSL.
2) redwoodctl detects wincred, calls helper to store token and then writes profiles.json on the NTFS mount.
3) concurrently, a background process (Windows-side redwoodctl auto-update or GUI) tries to refresh creds and writes via wincred too.
Result: sometimes profiles.json ends up with duplicate ids and conflicting expiry timestamps. localserve sees expired token in file and triggers a refresh, which races with the other process, causing repeated 401/refresh loops.

anya: can you paste the logs (redwoodctl -v localserve) showing the 401/refresh cycle?

mike: pasted trimmed logs:
```
[t=14:12:01] auth: token expired, starting refresh for profile dev-wsl
[t=14:12:01] credhelper: writing to wincred://dev-wsl -> OK
[t=14:12:01] file: write profiles.json -> OK
[t=14:12:02] auth: refresh failed: token mismatch (expected ts=171, saw ts=162)
[t=14:12:02] auth: requeue refresh -> attempt 2
[t=14:12:02] credhelper: write wincred://dev-wsl -> OK (new token)
[t=14:12:02] file: write profiles.json -> OK (duplicate id: dev-wsl-1)
[t=14:12:03] auth: refresh failed: token mismatch (expected ts=183, saw ts=162)
... loop ...
```

sam: yikes. That looks like two writers without coordination. Our design expects a single source-of-truth: either file OR helper. If both are present we should reconcile at read-time with timestamps and prefer the freshest credential rather than blindly writing.

anya: also mixing NTFS mounts can add weird write ordering; rename/atomic-write semantics differ. Two suggestions: 1) prefer an authoritative store per-OS (on WSL prefer file in WSL FS unless user opts in), 2) when writing detect concurrent modifications (stat + temp rename) and retry based on newest mtime.

mike: quick workaround: set `REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_HELPER=none` in WSL env so only file is used; that unblocks localserve.

ops: Created issue #820: "auth: handle multi-writer credential scenarios on hybrid windows/WSL setups; prefer freshest token and add write-retry/atomic rename for profiles.json"  https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/820

sam: I'll sketch a patch: on load, read helper + file; pick token with latest expires_at; on write, write temp + fsync + rename, and detect EEXIST/EINVAL/EACCES. If helper present, write helper then update file with same token, but if file changed in between, retry reconcile loop up to N times.

anya: also add docs note for WSL about not pointing XDG_CONFIG_HOME at NTFS unless you understand concurrent Windows processes. Add `REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_HELPER=none` example.

mike: added repro snippet to #820 and the env workaround. Thanks — local testing works again after turning off the helper. Closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
